title: Magha Puja
hookLine: in Thailand, Laos and Cambodia, the February or March full moon: 1,250 disciples gather unannounced
last: ASALHA PUJA — THE WHEEL STILL TURNS.

cards: No group chat. No invitation. No reminder the day before.
And still, everyone who mattered walks through the door. In ordinary life it hardly ever works that way. Tradition tells of a full moon when it did, on a remarkable scale.
Twelve hundred and fifty monks walked to the same grove on the same night, the story goes, and not one of them had been called.

teach.b: Magha Puja. Magha is the month whose full moon falls in February or March, and the day is kept especially in Thailand, Laos and Cambodia.

teach.h: FOUR THINGS AT THE BAMBOO GROVE.
teach.b: The story, as the commentaries tell it, happened at the Bamboo Grove near Rajagaha, in the first year of the Buddha's teaching. Four things came together, which is why the day is sometimes called the fourfold assembly.
It was the full moon of Magha. Twelve hundred and fifty monks arrived without being summoned. All of them were arahants, fully awakened.
And all had been ordained by the Buddha himself. To that gathering, the tradition says, the Buddha gave a short summary of the whole teaching, called the Ovada Patimokkha, the exhortation.
Its heart is a verse in the Dhammapada.

teach.h: NO SIN, DO GOOD, PURIFY THE MIND.
teach.b: In Max Muller's translation: "Not to commit any sin, to do good, and to purify one's mind", that, the verse says, is the teaching of the awakened ones. Three parts.
One common reading: the precepts, then giving and kindness, then meditation. Some teachers call it the whole teaching small enough to fit on a sticky note.

On Magha Puja night in Thailand, people gather at temples at dusk and walk around the main hall three times, holding a candle, incense and flowers, one circle each for the Buddha, the dhamma and the sangha.
Some Western communities keep a Sangha Day of their own in the same spirit. Look back over this week of holy days. Vesak: born, awake, gone.
Hanamatsuri: a clean beginning. Lanterns: light for the many. Culture or religion: both.
And tonight, the sangha, the people who came without being called.

how: On Magha Puja, especially in Thailand, Laos and Cambodia, Buddhists gather at temples at dusk and walk three times around the main hall carrying a candle, incense and flowers, and many keep the eight precepts and listen to teaching.

games.why: the verse at the heart of the Ovada Patimokkha, given at the Magha gathering: precepts, kindness, meditation.

practice: Picture the Bamboo Grove at moonrise, and monks walking in quietly from every direction, taking their seats.

Now bring to mind the people who practice alongside you, near or far, a friend, a teacher, a stranger at a temple, anyone doing this same thing today, and let them take their seats in the grove too. Rest in that company.
